I farm the full 34.1 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the system I know best and it fits my land and water conditions. I have done this for many years, and at my age I will keep the plan steady rather than take risks. Some people in my family work off-farm, so I want field work that is familiar, timely, and not too complicated. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on that to keep both crops stable in dry periods. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer up front with enough nitrogen to support tillering and grain filling, irrigate a few key times, and keep pesticide use limited but timely. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because it gives me steadier yield, use moderate fertilizer with enough nitrogen, irrigate when summer rain is not enough, and keep pest control simple. I will use rotary tillage because it saves labor and matches the wheat-maize cycle well on my farm. I am aiming for stable yield, manageable labor, and low risk, not chasing the very highest output.
